status: Complete; passed fresh independent grade at 8.0/10; ready for master integration handoff

source.provider: Purdue University official campus building footprint service
source.reference_status: Official campus-map polygon; not a certified survey.

secondary_visual_references.provider: Kappa Kappa Gamma, The Key, Vol. 69 No. 1 (February 1952), p.14
secondary_visual_references.use: Photo and caption identify Gamma Delta’s present home, describe white rostone and a French Provincial chapter home built in 1935. Visible two main facade levels, steep roof with dormers, repeated windows and shutters, and centered entry inform the broad form; no scaled measurements.

secondary_visual_references.provider: Kappa Kappa Gamma, Gamma Delta chapter history
secondary_visual_references.use: Historical narrative reports present site obtained in 1929 and Waldron Street home became a reality in 1936–37; conflicts slightly with 1952 magazine construction year.

secondary_visual_references.provider: Purdue University Fraternity, Sorority and Cooperative Life / Panhellenic Association
secondary_visual_references.use: Confirms Kappa Kappa Gamma Gamma Delta as a current Purdue chapter; no architectural data.

transform.axes: X east, Y north, Z up
transform.units: meters; local project approximation, not surveyed CRS

measurements.after_shell_base: All 12 transformed GIS ring points matched on reopen with 0.0 m maximum residual.
measurements.position_status: Base wall ring follows all 12 source points; source positional accuracy is unpublished.
measurements.plan_dimension_status: GIS polygon supports plan dimensions; its concave multi-wing shape is retained. Roof overhangs extend slightly beyond the source outline.
measurements.orientation_status: Long west-facing facade modeled from historical photo; street bearing and entry compass orientation are not verified.
measurements.height_status: Estimated 7.3 m eaves and 11.0 m ridge; no measured elevation source. GIS NUM_LEVELS=1 conflicts with two main facade levels visible in the historical photo; GIS field definition unknown.

geometry_edits: Rebuilt the assigned one-object massing library as a detailed mesh using the official FID 782 footprint ring as the exact ground-level base.
Added two main facade levels, repeated sash-window openings and muted-blue shutters based on the historical house photograph; their exact rhythm and dimensions are estimated.
Added a source-informed steep slate roof over the main mapped wing, a roof cap following the concave footprint, and three dormers.
Added a centered wood entry, simple portico, plinth, floor bands, and warm light stone trim based on the historical facade photo.
Removed unused original brick-texture image datablocks so the saved model has no external image dependencies.
Preserved assigned asset ID, manifest file path, collection name, object name, campus coordinate frame, and identity object transform.
uncertainties: Purdue campus GIS is not a certified survey and publishes no positional accuracy.
GIS NUM_LEVELS=1 conflicts with two main facade levels visible in the 1952 photo; field definition is undocumented.
Eaves and ridge heights, exact current roof plan, detailed facade rhythm, materials, and entry bearing are estimates or unverified.
1952 publication reports the house was built in 1935, while the Kappa history says the Waldron home became a reality in 1936–37. The source photo may predate later alterations.
No georeferenced elevation photo, measured floor plan, or contemporary surveyed facade was located.

independent_grade.summary: Exact concave GIS footprint and modular export pass. Height, roof detail, facade interpretation, and entry bearing remain uncertain; the one-level GIS attribute conflicts with the historical two-level photograph.
